_comment: Verbatim producer output. Bundle documents from `scripts/build_review_bundle.py --fixture --seed 424242`; `annotations` and `health` from a live `scripts/review_server.py` against that bundle. Do not hand-edit: regenerate it. See generated.test.ts for why.

documentation.raw_frac_10: UNcalibrated ensemble fraction at 10 min — the share of members whose cumulative max crosses the detection threshold by then, before the served isotonic curve. NaN off coverage.
documentation.raw_frac_20: UNcalibrated ensemble fraction at 20 min — the share of members whose cumulative max crosses the detection threshold by then, before the served isotonic curve. NaN off coverage.
documentation.raw_frac_30: UNcalibrated ensemble fraction at 30 min — the share of members whose cumulative max crosses the detection threshold by then, before the served isotonic curve. NaN off coverage.
documentation.raw_frac_45: UNcalibrated ensemble fraction at 45 min — the share of members whose cumulative max crosses the detection threshold by then, before the served isotonic curve. NaN off coverage.
documentation.raw_frac_60: UNcalibrated ensemble fraction at 60 min — the share of members whose cumulative max crosses the detection threshold by then, before the served isotonic curve. NaN off coverage.
documentation.obs_max_5km_mm_h: Maximum observed rain rate (mm/h) over the native-grid disc of radius 5 km centred on the station, from the same anchor field the cycle forecast from. NaN when no pixel of the disc is inside the composite.
documentation.up_max_20km_mm_h: Maximum observed rain rate (mm/h) in the upwind corridor 6 km wide and 0-20 km long, laid along the LOCAL completed flow at the station (upwind = opposite the direction the cells move). NaN when the corridor has no pixel inside the composite or the flow gives no usable direction.
documentation.up_max_40km_mm_h: The same maximum over the 0-40 km corridor.
documentation.up_dist_km: Distance along the corridor to the nearest pixel at or above 0.5 mm/h, in km, 0 when the station itself is wet. NaN when the 40 km corridor holds no such pixel ('no echo upwind') — the model turns that into an indicator plus a capped value rather than a large number.
documentation.up_wet_frac_40km: Share of the 40 km corridor's in-composite pixels at or above 0.5 mm/h. Separates a solid band from a ragged edge at the same maximum intensity.
documentation.bulk_kmh: Speed of the cycle's bulk storm motion (km/h) — the target the flow completion relaxes toward (dense_flow.MotionEstimate.bulk_vy/bulk_vx), converted with the frame's own pixel size and spacing.
documentation.bulk_dir_deg: Compass bearing the bulk motion is heading TOWARD: 0 = north, 90 = east. NaN when the bulk motion is below the usable-speed floor.
documentation.local_speed_kmh: Speed (km/h) of the COMPLETED flow at the station's own pixel — the field the forecast is advected with there, which off the echo is the completion's fill rather than a measurement.
documentation.stalled_share: Share of wet pixels whose RAW flow estimate is below 5 km/h (dense_flow.MotionEstimate.stalled_share). A per-cycle health signal for the H-F stall defect, constant across the cycle's stations.
documentation.season: 'summer' (May-Sep), 'winter' (Dec-Mar) or 'shoulder' (Apr, Oct, Nov), from the decision instant. The same split the threshold sweep and the Layer B strata use.
documentation.hour_utc: Hour of the decision instant in UTC, 0-23. The model uses it as sin/cos so 23 and 0 are adjacent.
documentation.frame_age_min: Minutes between the anchor frame's nominal time and the decision instant — the cycle's own simulated latency under the anchor policy, not a constant.
documentation.station_radar_km: Great-circle km from the station to the nearest DMI radar (product_pairs.nearest_radar_km). Constant per station; the composite under-detects close to a radar and over-reads column max far from one.

caveats.detail: The radar verdict comes from the same instrument the forecast was made from, so agreement is a consistency check and not an independent opinion.
The composite is column-max reflectivity, which biases the rate high: virga and bright band read as rain the gauge never sees.
A wet neighbour says rain existed in the area, not at this gauge.
An onset instant is a slot END, so the first drop fell in the preceding 10 minutes and every measured lead is biased that far negative.
The replay resets the engine at every coverage-run boundary, which hands out a re-arm the live service never had; those rows carry run_boundary_rearm.
The threshold table was fitted on these same months: the thresholds are in-sample (held_out=false).

observed.reduction: block p90 over 4x4 native 500 m pixels (national.observed_rain_grid); a block is nodata only when every native pixel in it is
observed.source: DMI column-max composite, Marshall-Palmer Z-R with the file's own zr-a/zr-b, capped at 53 dBZ and 100 mm/h (transform.dbz_to_rain_rate)
observed.caveat: column-max reflectivity biases the rate HIGH (tall cores, virga, bright band) — an upper-bound proxy for surface rain

overlay.alpha_ramp: transparent below 0.3 mm/h; alpha 70 -> 255 linear in log10(mm/h) from 0.3 to 2.0 mm/h; opaque above

verdicts.description: The forecast was wrong in a way a better model or rule could fix.
The forecast was defensible; the label came from the scoring rule — the onset definition, the matching window, the re-arm, a low-catch gauge, or coverage.
The evidence in the bundle does not settle it.

tag_groups.label: Why did it warn with no rain?

tags.description: Echo existed upstream (up_max_20/40km_mm_h > 0) and decayed before arrival. STEPS advects; it carries no deterministic growth or decay.
The echo passed to one side: the completed flow at the station (local_speed_kmh, bulk_dir_deg) differed from the cell's own motion.
The rain did come, but after sent + lead + tolerance, so the greedy matching window would not let this warning claim the onset.
The rain came before the warning could be useful; a neighbouring claim carries a large positive lead_error_min.
Column-max reflectivity over a dry gauge — the documented composite bias. Radar wet, gauge dry, neighbours dry.
Stationary echo across frames, or a high stalled_share; small station_radar_km (near-radar clutter) or large (melting layer).
Radar 0.5-1 mm/h; the gauge stayed below 0.1 mm per slot or below the 0.2 mm two-slot onset floor. Real rain, not a countable onset.
Neighbours wet, this gauge dry with known=true: wind loss, low catch, or a gauge not yet dead by the dead_gauges rule.
The window's slots are known=false. There is no truth here, and known_until / pending did not catch it.
Rain was already falling before the warning, so the onset rule's 60 dry minutes was never satisfied. The engine's already-raining test reads only the current row.
raw_frac_<lead> pinned at 1.0 — ensemble saturation; visible as p_rain much greater than p_post, or both pinned.
p_decision within 5 points of the threshold: a coin flip, not a mechanism. Tag it so it does not pollute the mechanism counts.
frame_age_min >= 20, or a coverage gap immediately before: the decision stood on an old composite.
observed_mm_h null, few valid pixels in the disc, or the station near a composite or radar edge.
Something else. Requires a note.
Disarmed at the onset with the 60-minute re-arm unexpired: structurally unreachable. If this is a large share of misses, the finding is a rule change, not a model change.
The arm was consumed silently by the already-raining branch before the onset — no push, still disarmed.
p_decision peaked below the threshold across the whole pre-onset window: sharpness or calibration, not plumbing.
Both p_post and p_rain were null at the rule's lead, so the engine passed over those rows (off coverage, unserved lead, feature gap).
Nothing upstream at -30 min (up_max_40km_mm_h near zero, up_dist_km NaN): the rain grew in place, which advection cannot see.
Rain was upstream but arrived sooner than the lead could cover: small up_dist_km with high bulk_kmh.
frame_age_min plus the arrival time exceeded the lead. A fresher anchor would have warned.
Decision rows are missing around the onset even though the coverage rule did not call it uncovered.
The disc stayed dry through the onset: beam overshoot or shallow rain, typically at large station_radar_km.
An isolated 0.2 mm with no radar and no neighbour: a suspect onset (heated gauge, dew, a bumped bucket).
Winter, long precip duration with tiny depth, weak radar: the Z-R relation is rain-tuned.
The 'new' onset is a continuation whose dry run was reset by an UNKNOWN slot rather than a dry one.
Peak p_decision within 5 points below the threshold.
Something else. Requires a note.
The +/-90 minute window or the 2 km product grid was not enough to judge this one. Candidate for a --deepen re-run.
Worth coming back to, or worth showing someone.

prologue.note: A disarmed subscription re-arms only after 60 minutes of radar time below threshold, and any over-threshold row resets that clock while disarmed. minutes_to_rearm is null when the clock is not running at all.

gauge.onset_rule: first wet slot after 60 min known dry, delivering 0.2 mm over it and the slot after it

radar_disc.statistic: p90 over the disc, as the service samples it

neighbours.caveat: A wet neighbour says rain existed in the area, not that it rained at this station.

dual_truth.rule: gauge: a wet slot in the window; radar: the disc at or above 0.5 mm/h in the window; neighbour: any gauge within 20 km wet in the window
dual_truth.caveat: The radar verdict comes from the instrument that made the forecast; agreement is a consistency check, not a second opinion. A wet neighbour says rain existed in the area.
